goals: Expose exact component-bearing Matcha Flavoured recipe and non-recipe identities through JEI without duplicating JEI's vanilla recipe ownership.
Build a shared exact catalog from effective, post-resolution Matcha recipe outputs and conservative C3 non-recipe identities for both JEI and Creative Search.
Keep Matcha recipe knowledge idempotent and server-owned while JEI remains an optional client integration.
scope: Preserve the accepted C2 baseline: seven JEI vanilla recipe categories, ten audited Matcha recipe namespaces, 315 exact component-bearing output ingredients, and idempotent server-side recipe awards.
Maintain C3's data-driven Matcha Villager Trades and Matcha Acquisition categories with 175 supported trade pages, 249 conservative acquisition pages, and 240 exact non-recipe identities.

Retain the exact JEI 30.18.0.144 subtype boundary: skip all 14 JEI-owned base interpreters, use the companion-owned exact-stack bridge for 19 identities, and keep the accepted component-manifest path for the other 221.

Preserve C4's effective post-resolution recipe catalog so compatibility replacements such as Blessing of Demeter remain authoritative. C7 contributes exact Matcha stacks additively and idempotently without rebuilding or clearing global Creative Search, while suppressing only the plain default food identities canonically replaced by a synchronized Matcha effect-bearing ordinary-food stack.

exclusions: JEI patches, replacement of JEI-owned subtype interpreters, duplicate or fake vanilla recipes, and fabricated recipes for non-recipe mechanics.

Inventory, menu, slot, quick-move, general creative-validation, Trinkets, Inventory Extended, Offhand, or Carried behavior changes; C7 contributes exact Matcha stacks and only tracks/restores narrowly matched plain default food discovery identities in Creative Search and optional JEI.
Contextual exploration-map trades, unsupported identity-changing loot functions, exact loot odds, and live villager demand, reputation, or exhaustion state.
A dedicated-server-without-JEI validation claim; that runtime gate remains explicitly unperformed.

state.milestone: Exact C4 has a user-reported external runtime FAIL for incomplete global Creative Search. Exact C6 now also has a user-reported external runtime FAIL: Creative/JEI exposed both the plain/default and Matcha-aware variants of affected foods, including minecraft:glow_berries and Matcha's Glow Berry Mash on minecraft:rotten_flesh. C7 preserves C4's effective catalog and C5's no-global-rebuild safety architecture. It selects canonical replacements only from synchronized Matcha catalog stacks on ordinary food bases whose patched minecraft:consumable has effects, including effect-only glow berries, preserves custom-model and unrelated component variants, filters category Search sources before vanilla indexes them, and retries payload reconciliation once the play client is ready. C7 is static-pass and runtime-untested; C5 is not classified as failed. Accepted C3's external PASS remains bound only to C3, C2 remains rollback/provenance, and the dedicated-server-without-JEI gate remains unperformed.

current.summary: Keeps one Matcha-aware representative for effect-bearing ordinary foods in Creative Search and JEI.
